### Is this a reproducible bug?

- [x] I confirm this is a reproducible bug, not a feature request, idea, question, contribution proposal, or direction check.

### Current behavior

After `herdr server live-handoff`, every pane under the new server loses macOS responsible-process attribution. Anything that shells out to `op` (1Password CLI integration) prompts on every call with no "Always Allow" option, since 1Password can't resolve a signed ancestor to bind consent to. It hits migrated panes and freshly opened ones, so it's the server, not the pane. Normally-launched session servers are fine.

The handoff server runs reparented to launchd outside the normal launch path:
`16529  1  herdr server --handoff-import .../herdr-handoff-96840.sock ...`

macOS sets a process's responsible process at spawn, and TCC/app integrations use it to persist consent. The handoff spawn never establishes a signed responsible ancestor, so the whole subtree is unattributable. This probably affects other TCC-gated access too (camera, mic, automation), not just 1Password.

Different from #516, which is about the `(deleted)` exe path, not attribution.

### Expected behavior

Panes under a handed-off server attribute to a signed responsible app the same way a normally-launched server does, so 1Password offers "Always Allow" and consent persists.

### Reproduction

1. macOS with 1Password desktop CLI integration on. In a normal herdr session, run something that calls `op` in a pane (`op whoami`, or chezmoi in account mode). 1Password prompts once and "Always Allow" sticks.
2. `herdr server live-handoff`.
3. Run the same `op` command in any pane under the new server, including a newly opened one. It prompts every time with no "Always Allow".

### Impact

live-handoff is the recommended way to keep panes across an upgrade, but its server ends up tainted for anything needing macOS app authorization. There's no in-place fix. The only workaround is moving work to a fresh session and dropping the handed-off one, which defeats the point of handoff.

### Environment

- Herdr version: 0.7.1
- Update channel: stable
- Operating system: macOS (Darwin 25.5.0), Apple Silicon
- Terminal: herdr panes (reproduces regardless of host terminal)
- Shell, if relevant: zsh
- Relevant config: 1Password CLI 2.34.1 + 1Password 8 desktop integration; chezmoi in 1Password account mode

comments.body:
Hitting the same root cause on 0.8.0 / macOS 26.6.1, but from a different trigger. Adding what we found in case it helps.

### It also happens without handoff

An incoming `herdr --remote <host>` stops a healthy server and starts its own in its place. We never passed `--handoff`, and the server log has no handoff lines. From `herdr-server.log`:

```
20:28:28  app.startup pid=73792   <- started by the terminal app
20:28:49  incoming SSH session (no tty)
20:28:53  server shutdown initiated, 8 panes SIGHUPed
20:28:53  app.startup pid=75855   <- replacement, 0.5s later
20:28:54  client connected
```

The old server reported the terminal app as its responsible process. The new one reports itself. So it is not only `live-handoff` — any path that rebuilds the server outside the app can taint it, and a plain remote attach does it without the user asking for a handoff.

### It breaks local network access too

You expected other TCC-gated things to break. They do. In a pane, non-Apple binaries cannot reach the LAN:

| from a pane, same LAN target | result |
| --- | --- |
| `/usr/bin/curl`, `nc`, `/usr/bin/python3` | works |
| Homebrew `python3`, `kubectl` | `EHOSTUNREACH`, immediately |
| same non-Apple binary to the internet | works |

Apple binaries are exempt from Local Network Privacy, so `curl` and `ping` keep working. That makes this easy to misread as a network problem.

### One correction: reparenting to launchd is not the cause

The report says the handoff server is tainted because it runs "reparented to launchd outside the normal launch path". We tested that part specifically. A process started by a granted `.app` that double-forks, calls `setsid` and ends up at `ppid=1` keeps its attribution and its LAN access. So does a chain through setuid `/usr/bin/login -flp`. Only who spawned it matters. A fix based on avoiding reparenting would not help.

### How to check it

```sh
python3 -c 'import ctypes,sys
f=ctypes.CDLL("/usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib").responsibility_get_pid_responsible_for_pid
f.argtypes=[ctypes.c_int]; f.restype=ctypes.c_int; print(f(int(sys.argv[1])))' <server-pid>
```

A healthy server prints the app's pid. A tainted one prints its own pid. No root needed, so it may be usable as a test assertion.

### Why there is no way to recover

Once the server is its own responsible process, macOS looks up a bundle id for it and finds none. `codesign -dv` reports `Signature=adhoc`, `TeamIdentifier=not set`, `Info.plist=not bound`. The system log shows that lookup working for a normal app (`LocalNetwork: found bundle id <app> by PID`) and never firing for herdr. With no bundle id, herdr never appears in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Local Network, so there is nothing to allow and no prompt is possible. It just fails silently.

Embedding an `Info.plist` with a bundle id would at least make a self-responsible server grantable, separately from fixing the restart path.

### Note on #1422

#1422 looks like this same bug reported as a LAN symptom. It was closed as "not a herdr bug — stale server with a bad cached Local Network decision". There is nothing cached against the server, because it has no identity to cache a decision against. Restarting fixed it there because the new server happened to be started from a granted app. It will probably come back.

Adding measurements to this from an independent reproduction today (2026-08-21) — the attribution-loss mechanism, with a probe-verified fix direction.

# herdr: detached server daemon makes all pane children un-grantable under macOS Local Network Privacy

**Environment:** macOS Tahoe (25.6.0), herdr 0.8.2 (`detached_server_daemon: true`), terminal: par-term (Local Network **allowed**), leaf tools: bun (signed), node (Developer ID signed).

**Impact:** Every process spawned in a herdr pane is silently blocked from LAN sockets (EHOSTUNREACH / fetch failures) — regardless of the terminal's Local Network grant or the child binary's own signature. Anything routed through a multiplexer pane (LLM proxies, self-hosted memory/API servers, MCP servers on the LAN) breaks with "Unable to connect" while the identical command in a plain terminal tab works. `/mcp reload`-style reconnects can never fix it.

**Root cause (measured):** herdr's server runs detached (PPID 1). macOS Local Network Privacy grants attach to a *responsible app*; pane processes trace responsibility to the orphaned daemon, which has no grantable identity. Apple-signed system tools pass (exempt); signed third-party binaries under the daemon are still blocked.

**Evidence that a fix works (measured with a probe app):**
- An LSUIElement app bundle whose own binary opens a LAN socket triggers the LNR prompt, becomes grantable, and passes after Allow (`APP-OWN-SOCKET: OK`).
- After granting, a spawned child process also passes (`CHILD-BUN: OK`) — bundle grants propagate to children.
- Caveat: ad-hoc re-signing the bundle invalidated one grant binding in our tests; a stable signature matters.

**Suggested fix:** offer a mode where the herdr server is hosted inside an app bundle (LSUIElement background app, stable signature) instead of orphaning to init, so one Local Network grant covers every pane. The remaining open question for a real build is whether bundle attribution survives herdr's daemonize step — the probe's child was a direct child, and daemonize-fork survival wasn't testable externally.

**Workarounds in the meantime:** run LAN-dependent sessions in a plain terminal tab outside herdr, or per-service SSH tunnels to localhost (localhost is LNR-exempt).
+1 to also have this address! Thank you and appreciate the work done so far!

I confirm this bug on herdr 0.8.2 and macOS 26.5.1, with `detached_server_daemon: true`. I add two items that the thread does not show yet. The first is a control experiment. It isolates the attribution to the parent process. The second is a trap that can make a second machine look unaffected.

## 1. A granted GUI app as parent isolates the attribution

The reproductions to now compare "inside a pane" with "plain terminal". This leaves the terminal app as a variable.

A better control keeps the binary and the target constant. It changes only the parent process. One of the parents must already hold a Local Network grant.

The script, the binary, and the target stay the same. Only the parent changes.

| parent | result |
| --- | --- |
| `sshd` | connects |
| Emacs (GUI app, Local Network **allowed**) | connects |
| herdr pane | **fails, `Errno 65` / `EHOSTUNREACH`** |

This is the script:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
/run/current-system/sw/bin/python3 -c "
import socket
try:
    s = socket.create_connection((\"<LAN_IP>\", 8080), 4); print(\"OK connect\"); s.close()
except Exception as e: print(\"FAIL\", type(e).__name__, e)
"
```

To run it under Emacs, use `emacsclient -e '(shell-command-to-string "/tmp/conn.sh")'`. To run it under a pane, use `herdr pane run <pane> /tmp/conn.sh`.

`sshd` alone is a weak control, because macOS makes it exempt. The Emacs row gives the information. A normal GUI app can hold a grant. It then gives that grant to an unsigned child process. herdr cannot do this, because it has no entry to grant. The child process does not change between the rows.

The report above is correct on signatures. An ad hoc signature on the child does not help. I made a copy of the same binary with `codesign -s -`. From a pane, the copy still returned `No route to host`. The grant must attach to the responsible ancestor.

Two more measurements show the exemption boundary. I made both from one pane. Both aimed at a host with no service on the port.

- `/usr/bin/python3` returns `ConnectionRefusedError` (`Errno 61`)
- nix `python3` returns `OSError Errno 65`

The routing is the same. The results are opposite. This test removes routing and source-address selection early. macOS reports the denial as `EHOSTUNREACH`. For this reason, an incorrect diagnosis is easy here.

## 2. A transparent proxy can hide this problem

Read this section if you compare two machines.

I had a second Mac that looked unaffected. On that Mac, the same CLI reached the same LAN service from a pane. The Mac was not unaffected. It runs a transparent proxy (Surge or mihomo). The proxy holds the Local Network grant. The proxy therefore carries the traffic for the CLI.

To find this condition, point the tool at an address with no device. A proxy then answers at the HTTP layer. Without a proxy, you get a connection error.

```
$ TOOL_API_URL=http://<nonexistent-LAN-IP>:8080 tool status
error: /health returned 503: <!doctype html> ...
```

A host that does not exist cannot send a 503 page. Only a proxy can send it. On that same Mac, nix `python3` and `node` still failed from a pane with `Errno 65`. This result agrees with all the other machines. The Mac is not a counter-example. The behaviour is consistent.

Check for a proxy before you use any machine as a working reference.

## Environment

- herdr 0.8.2 (Homebrew), stable channel, `live_handoff: true`, `detached_server_daemon: true`
- macOS 26.5.1, Apple Silicon
- herdr binary: bare Mach-O, `flags=0x20002(adhoc,linker-signed)`, `TeamIdentifier=not set`, no `.app` bundle
- Affected child processes: an unsigned Rust CLI, nix `python3`, nix `node`
- Not affected: Apple platform binaries (`/usr/bin/curl`, `/usr/bin/python3`)

The LSUIElement bundle solution above agrees with my measurements. I can do either experiment again on a test build.

I was connecting to a remote macOS box using herdr (`herdr machine add ...`) and was running into the same issue with local network access permissions. In this scenario, herdr's parent process is sshd, a platform binary, and the OS doesn't even show a "local network permission" prompt and denies every local network connection.

I ended up creating a simple "Herdr.app" app bundle which launches `herdr server`, launched the server through it, then granted the "Herdr" app local network access permission.
I would also suggest updating the issue title to not specifically mention 1password. The issue is definitely more general than that, and I missed it the first time I was searching the issue list.

Additional data point confirming this, with a diagnostic signature that may help others identify it.

**Setup:** three Apple Silicon Macs, all **macOS 27.0.1**, herdr 0.9.3 (MacPorts), server started via **plain SSH login / headless** (no live-handoff involved) — so the title's "remote attach, detached daemon" case. Target services live on a **ZeroTier private subnet (172.30.0.0/16)** behind a DNS zone served over the same subnet. A fourth machine still on macOS 26.6.2 with the same setup is unaffected — enforcement appears to have tightened in 27.

**Symptom:** every network client inside herdr panes fails to reach the private-subnet services, with *inconsistent error flavors* depending on the client library (ENOTFOUND, ECONNREFUSED, hangs) — which made it look like a DNS or service problem for weeks. Restarting panes or starting brand-new processes under the same server doesn't help; the same commands over a plain SSH shell on the same machine work.

**Discriminating signature**, from inside a failing pane:

```
$ curl -v --max-time 6 https://<name-on-private-subnet>/ -o /dev/null
* IPv4: 172.30.76.174
*   Trying 172.30.76.174:443...
* Immediate connect fail for 172.30.76.174: No route to host
* connect to 172.30.76.174 port 443 from 172.30.32.143 port 60300 failed: No route to host
* Failed to connect ... after 12 ms
```

The tells: (1) **instant** EHOSTUNREACH (~12 ms, not a timeout) (2) on a route the kernel demonstrably has — it already bound the correct private-subnet **source** address — (3) while the identical curl over an SSH login succeeds. That combination is the NECP policy-deny signature of Local Network privacy, not routing. Also note `dscacheutil`/getaddrinfo keep resolving *inside* the pane (queries are proxied through mDNSResponder, which isn't subject to the caller's attribution), so DNS working while TCP gets "No route to host" is expected under this bug, and is why client libraries surface such different errors.

Ruled out before attributing: no proxy env vars in the pane; `curl --noproxy '*'` fails identically; zone is v4-only (no Happy-Eyeballs artifact).

Can confirm the workaround in the thread: stopping the server and starting `herdr server` from a GUI terminal app (which holds the Local Network grant) restores pane connectivity — children inherit the terminal's attribution. For headless machines that never see a GUI login, there's no way to trigger or inherit the consent prompt at all, which makes the signed-bundle identity (thanks @paulrobello for the gist) the only durable path; we're packaging a variant of it downstream.

Also hitting this with the desktop app: Herdr.app 0.1.12, herdr-core (hc) 0.1.17, macOS 27.2 (26B123).

Herdr.app starts `herdr-core connect`, which spawns `herdr-core --hc-launchd`; that process reparents to launchd (PPID 1) and owns every pane. From a pane, Bun gets `ECONNREFUSED` on an HTTPS endpoint on the LAN and `EHOSTUNREACH` on `172.27.10.2:22`, while `/usr/bin/curl` from the same pane reaches it. An MCP client running in the pane fails to load its LAN server on every start.

Neither binary can ask for Local Network access: Herdr.app has no `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription`, and `~/.local/bin/herdr-core` has no Info.plist, so macOS denies without a prompt and there is nothing to toggle in Privacy & Security. #5406 looked like the right fix; it would be great to see it land.

Adding an independent reproduction on the desktop app, including the probe from @ciiiii and one detail that may save others a dead end: `tccutil` cannot reset this.

## Environment

- macOS 27.2 (26B123), Apple Silicon
- Herdr.app 0.1.12, herdr-core 0.1.17, `herdr` CLI 0.9.5
- Fresh session started from the app. **No `live-handoff`, no `--remote`, no `herdr server` invocation** — so this is not limited to handoff.

## Symptom

From a pane, LAN targets fail immediately while the internet works:

| command (same pane, same target `<lan-host>:443`) | result |
| --- | --- |
| `/usr/bin/curl` | 200, valid cert |
| `/usr/bin/nc`, `/usr/bin/openssl s_client` | connect OK |
| `/usr/bin/perl`, `/usr/bin/ruby` | connect OK |
| pyenv `python3` | `EHOSTUNREACH` |
| Homebrew `node` | `EHOSTUNREACH` |
| `git` → `/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/.../git-remote-http` | `EHOSTUNREACH` |
| any of the above to `github.com` | works |

Kernel log for a failing attempt:

```
tcp drop outgoing [<client-ip>:50342 <-> <lan-host>:443] interface: en0
```

Versus `tcp connected` for curl. So it is dropped on egress per process, not a network fault.

## Probe confirms the server is self-responsible

Using the snippet from @ciiiii on the running core:

```
core responsible_pid = 11854   # 11854 is the core itself
```

TCC attribution for pane children names the core, not the app:

```
responsible={TCCDProcess: identifier=dev.herdr.core, pid=1638,
  responsible_path=~/.local/bin/herdr-core,
  binary_path=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/libexec/git-core/git-remote-http}
```

For reference, the core has no bundle to resolve to, and it does not live inside the app bundle:

```
$ codesign -dv ~/.local/bin/herdr-core
Identifier=dev.herdr.core
Authority=Developer ID Application: Herdr, Inc. (2W9652Q7QR)
Info.plist=not bound

$ ls ~/Applications/Herdr.app/Contents
CodeResources  MacOS/Herdr  Resources/Herdr.icns  Resources/LICENSE  Resources/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES  Info.plist
```

And nehelper cannot resolve the coalition at all:

```
symptomsd: Can't lookup UUID ... for procname (null), coalition dev.herdr.core.1216 nehelper (null)
nehelper:  Populating the cache with 1 UUID(s) for dev.herdr.app   # nothing for dev.herdr.core
```

## `tccutil` is a dead end on this build

Local Network is not a TCC service here, so the usual advice fails:

```
$ sudo tccutil reset LocalNetwork
tccutil: Failed to reset LocalNetwork

$ strings /usr/bin/tccutil | grep -i localnetwork
(no match)
```

It is enforced by nehelper network-privacy path rules instead (`com.apple.preferences.networkprivacy-…`, `PathRuleDefaultNonSystemIdentifier`). Worth adding to the troubleshooting guidance so nobody spends time on a reset that cannot work.

## The server always detaches, even on CLI starts

Every GUI-session start goes through the one-shot launchd job, so there is no way to keep the core in the app's coalition:

```
launchd: gui/501/dev.herdr.core.9462.1793729520888575000: Successfully spawned herdr-core[9465]
launchd: ... exited due to exit(0), ran for 17ms
```

Consequence: `ppid=1` and its own responsibility, as expected per the skill's "desktop starts use a one-shot launchd job".

I tried `HC_LAUNCHD_DIRECT=1` in case it forced the direct-child path described in the skill. The variable **is** inherited by the bridge (verified via `ps eww`), but the core still starts with `--hc-launchd` and the LAN remains blocked. If that variable is meant to be a supported escape hatch, it does not work; if it is internal, it may be worth noting that it looks like one.

## Not terminal-specific

The same failure reproduces in a second third-party terminal (OxideTerm 2.3.0, ad-hoc signed), while Apple's Terminal.app is unaffected — consistent with only the responsible app's grant mattering.

## Workaround in use

LAN `git` runs in Terminal.app. Inside Herdr only Apple SIP binaries get out, which is the misleading part: `curl` succeeding makes it look like a server problem rather than an attribution problem.

## Why this matters for #5406

The `Herdr Server.app` helper in #5406 is the only approach that can produce a grantable identity; the probe result above is exactly the before-state it is meant to change. Happy to re-test a build and report the responsibility pid plus the LAN result.

Same on herdr 0.9.5 / macOS 27.2, with a server herdr started by itself: `launchctl managername` → `Background`, and Homebrew `node` in panes can't reach the LAN. Starting `herdr server` explicitly from the terminal app works around it, but the grant is lost again after `herdr update` or a reboot, because the ad-hoc signing identifier changes with every build. Could a maintainer take over the signed-helper approach from #5406? It looks like the durable fix.

title: macOS: herdr server has no grantable app identity, so panes lose Local Network access and TCC consent (live-handoff, remote attach, detached daemon)
